title: "Couch-to-5k" or Couch to Ouch to Couch!? Who Takes Part in Beginner Runner Programmes in the UK and Is Non-Completion Linked to Musculoskeletal Injury?
authors: Relph N, Taylor SL, Christian DL, Dey P, Owen MB
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
population: Adults in a modified 9-week Couch-to-5k programme in the UK (mean age 47.1, 81.8% female, mean BMI 28.1, 64% with prior running experience)
findings: 110 runners (mean age 47.1 +/- 13.7 y; 81.8% female; mean BMI 28.1 kg/m2) did a modified 9-week Couch-to-5k programme; questionnaires at start, middle and end plus interviews with 15 drop-outs.
21 injuries were reported during the programme (19%); a previous injury increased the risk of a new injury (OR 7.56, 95% CI 2.06 to 27.75).
Only 27.3% completed the programme; dropping out was linked to musculoskeletal injury and to the progressive design of the programme.
64% of the sample had previous running experience and were classified as active; half self-reported pain or discomfort at baseline (EQ-5D-5L).
The authors state that Couch-to-5k lacks an evidence base and that future programmes should include injury-prevention advice and more flexible designs.
limitations: Small, single-arm, no comparator (so it cannot say whether run-walk beats 3 x 20 or 3 x 30 continuous); wide OR interval; the programme was 'modified' and the modifications are not in the abstract; self-selected sample.
implications: A run-walk plan is not shown to be safe by this study: 21 injuries (19%) and 27.3% completion mean the plan should allow repeating a week and should flag a prior injury.
A recent injury flag should lower the start dose or block the 3 x 20 floor (OR 7.56 is imprecise, so use as direction only, grade C).
Build in flexibility (repeat or hold a week) rather than a fixed 9-week ladder.
Couch-to-5k style plans are a convention without an evidence base; present the starter plan as a conservative default and not as evidence-based.
Ask about previous injury at onboarding and slow the starter plan for those who report one (OR 7.56, wide CI).
Allow repeating a week or pausing: the progressive design was linked to dropout, which supports a flexible progression rather than a fixed calendar.
